Order on Leave to Appeal Application No.... of 2023 1.

Heard Shri Manju Thakur, learned AGA-I for the State-appellant and Shri Shiv Kumar Pal,
learned counsel for the respondents.
2.

This application has been filed praying for granting leave to the State of U.P. for filing the instant Government Appeal against the impugned judgment and order dated 20.10.2022 whereby the respondents were acquitted for the offence under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 3. Learned AGA-I for the State submits that the trial court has committed manifest error of law in acquitting the respondents for committing offences under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act and also under the alternative Sections of 302 and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

Learned AGA-I for the State has submitted that the death of the deceased took place within seven years of her marriage in abnormal circumstances and, therefore, the court below ought not to have acquitted the accused persons.

4. Learned counsel for the respondents points out that all the witnesses for prosecution had turned hostile and none of them have supported the prosecution case at all, hence, the order passed by the trial court is justified since there was no evidence against the respondents before the trial court.
It is further submitted that respondent No.2 has also died after the judgment of the trial court.
5. After hearing the rival contentions, this Court does not find any ground to admit the appeal.
Judgment and order of acquittal passed by the trial court is in accordance with law.
6. Hence the above noted application is rejected.
Since the leave to appeal application has been rejected, this appeal is also dismissed.

Order Date :- 9.9.2024 Karan  State Of U.P. vs Dharmesh S/O Ramprasad And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177708790/
